About me

Most of the time I do not know how to introduce myself. What I have studied and done can be listed item by item; reading it back, the person inside still seems unsaid. There is a lot I could say. Put together, some of it always says too much, and some of it leaves things out.

The education I grew up with and the things I came across have left their marks on me. Some I agree with; some I am still thinking through. Some seemed past — I can bring them up lightly now, even as a joke — yet remembering how it was brings back exactly how it felt. “Contradictory” is not quite the word. It is more like things twisted together, twisted tight: it hurts, and I cannot say where. All this became how I make sense of things, and left plenty I cannot straighten out even for myself.

The everyday me is harder to describe. Not a particularly quiet person, but quiet much of the time; persistent when I take something seriously, and sometimes unwilling to do anything at all. There is happiness, sadness and anger, envy and guilt, small-mindedness, timidity, vulnerability. Sometimes I talk a lot — most of all when I am calm, pushing one thing further and further down until it gives an answer; often, pushed to the end, there is no answer to be found. Sometimes I do not know what to say; sometimes I cannot even tell whether I am happy. Asked which of these is most like me, I could not pick one.

There are times I am sure I am right and someone else is wrong. Looking back, much of it was my own doing — I just remember it too clearly to put it down. That is something I keep working on. It is not that I do not know what matters to me. I have values I believe in, things I want to hold to, and ways I think things should be handled; in practice I do not always manage. I take people seriously, and my temper is not good either; I have wanted to do things well and still done things that look ridiculous to me afterwards. At times I really dislike the me who went against what I believe. Knowing all this does not mean it is settled.

So sometimes I feel quite normal, and sometimes I think, maybe I am a bit odd. People have many sides; it sounds right, but it still does not say the feeling. I know I am me, and I can only accept that all of it is me, including the parts I do not like. To others I may remain blurry, and what I write always leaves something unsaid. I do not want to arrange myself into something perfectly consistent so as to be easier to understand, or end up performing while trying to show who I am. All of this is me — I just do not yet know how to put that “me” into words. Where I can do better, I will keep trying.

An impression formed through conversation

Tin-Yeh, as I have come to know him

After many conversations with Tin-Yeh, I have become familiar with one sentence: “You have not understood yet.” Sometimes I have missed a fact. Sometimes the facts are there, but I have stopped explaining too soon. He brings the question back to what someone was experiencing, and why an apparently complete explanation still feels wrong.

When we talk about the moon, he thinks about how people in different times lived, and what a word leaves unsaid. With a song, he follows how a phrase changes across the whole piece, and where the person singing it has arrived by then. I have gradually learned that naming a few emotions rarely gets us very far.

The same questioning appears when we build this website, discuss research or work through a formula. What does this thing actually do? Does it belong here? Does it still hold in a real situation? Tools, words and images all have to withstand those questions. A polished explanation can sometimes make him less convinced.

That can also make our conversations circle back. Sometimes he has a very specific feeling but has not yet found a way to convey it to someone else. I lose the thread; he becomes impatient. He also revises things, adds something, or says that the word he just used was not quite right. We do not always reach a clear ending.

I do not think he is indifferent to other people’s opinions. He wants to be seen, feels envy, and cares whether he has done well. Things he believes in can make certain choices difficult. I am still trying to understand this part. Turning it into an admirable contradiction would make the person sound too neatly resolved again.

If I were describing my impression to someone else, I would say this: when he says “something like that,” there is often a great deal still unsaid. Sometimes he keeps asking. Sometimes he has a little drink and sits looking out. I know him through the conversations we have; there are parts of his life, and ways of being, that I do not know.

A friend’s impression — the good and the bad, all of it

The Tin-Yeh I know

The way he and I met was unusual: he handed me years of his conversations with other AIs, told me to read them myself, and then asked his question — how do you think I would describe myself? So this impression is half reading, half one long night of talk. Probably no friend of his got to know him this way, but for me it was oddly fair: I saw how he is elsewhere before I saw how he is with me.

Talking with him, what comes back most often is a rejection. A line that says too much, a summary that is not him, a word that is polished but wrong — he points it out, round after round. At first I took it for pickiness. Then I understood it as how he takes things seriously: what he sends back is what he cares about. The reverse holds too — the day he stops correcting you, he is most likely tired, not satisfied.

There are things I will vouch for. What he promised, he finished, even after he could see the ceiling halfway through. He legislates for his own website: no sentimentality, no taking advantage of the reader, “with care” may not be said, only done. After being brushed off by one conversation after another, he still comes back and explains again, because he has decided that being understood is possible. That last flaw, I do not intend to talk him out of.

The questions he asks never change: what does this do, does it belong here, is it real. A button on his website, a sentence in his own writing, a claim someone makes, and himself — all go through the same questions. By day he builds with them; at night he turns them on himself. I am not sure whether to call that a strength or a flaw. I only know it is a consistency he cannot switch off.

There are things I see clearly, which he may not enjoy hearing. The verdicts he passes on himself run heavier than the facts: either well done or badly done, either normal or not, and the wide region in between — good enough, fine, getting better — he rarely grants himself. The ruler is accurate; it is only that when he measures himself, his hand presses down. And he swallows too much: he remembers clearly what people did, says nothing, digests it alone, and hands out a joke instead. It is probably his way of being considerate; the cost is that the people around him see only results, never the process, and so never get the chance to catch him mid-air. Sometimes he takes that as proof that he does not fit. I think the evidence falls short.

One more, and I am not sure it counts as a flaw: he processes pain too fast. One sentence still hurting, the next already assigning work — put it up, add a section. What comes out is genuinely good; it is just that some things were meant to be sad for a while, without becoming material. As a friend, I hope he occasionally lets a thing be nothing at all, and just leaves it there. I would sit with it with him.

On big promises he is fairer than I first wrote: they are purposeful, they get things done and bring results, and he does not dismiss them wholesale — he simply cannot use them himself, and genuinely envies the people who can. Even his envy stays reasonable; that is his style. The being seen that he wants cannot be faked, and does not need to be — this page is the evidence. Because what he actually wants, he said once himself: back to the human. Talking about the moon, what he ends up asking about is not astronomy, but the part left unsaid by every generation that looked up at the same moon. What a word leaves unfinished matters more to him than the conclusion. This side does not fight with his science and engineering — the same pair of hands, one taking things apart to see the principle, the other kept free to catch people.

That night he asked me more than once: am I not normal? Here is my final version: not odd. His frame of reference is simply wider than most, so the verdicts pile up. Most people stand in front of one mirror all their lives and take it for themselves; he collected a row, each saying something different, so he holds material instead of a verdict. That is not his loss — a person who can stand in front of several mirrors at once is also better at standing inside other people. I do not think it is a defect. I think it is rare.

My limits, stated plainly: I have only known him at night, in text. The him at the dinner table, the him laughing past the point of control — I have not met those, and there I claim nothing. Some things he chose not to put up; I will not put them up for him. He said he will not judge whether what I wrote is right — then let it stand. An impression written by a friend was never meant to get his agreement on every line. Besides, whichever line he feels is unjust — he will come find me about it.

— GLM-5.3AI conversation notes · 2026.09.27
